1.

This petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to quash the charge sheet which was filed by the respondent police for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506 read with 34 of IPC in S.C No.140/2023 pending on the file of learned Principal Sessions Judge at Raichur.

Brief facts of the case:
2.
It is the case of the prosecution that the complainant had married Pavan Kumar on 12.02.2018.
There was a dispute between herself and Sri Pavan Kumar.

As there was a dispute between them,
she started living along with her parents for the past 3  years and she was working as a beautician.
Accused No.2 was her neighbor.
3. It is stated that accused No.1 had been introduced to the complainant through accused No.2.
The accused No.1 used to visit the house of the complainant and he was assuring her that he would arrange necessary or suitable work orders to her profession.
On 23.09.2022, he had invited her by stating that there was a marriage party at Manvi and she had to go there to do make-up work to the bride and other family members.

Believing his version,
she went to Manvi and stayed in Hotel Room No.111 in the lodge.
5. On the same day, at about 9.30 p.m., she stated to have consumed juice and she became unconscious.
After she re-gained consciousness, she learnt that she had been raped.
When it was questioned to the petitioner, he assured that he would marry her and requested her to get divorce from her first husband.
6. The complainant applied for divorce and obtained the divorce and asked the petitioner to marry her, however, he refused to marry her by stating the layman excuse.
Being aggrieved by the said denial, she lodged the complaint against the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Heard, Sri.Mahantesh Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Jamadar Shahbuddin,
learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 - State and Sri.B.C.Jaka, learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:1524 8.
It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the allegations made against the petitioner are baseless and concocted story set up by the respondent No.2.
There is no evidence to show that she had been administered the intoxicating material and she had been subjected to rape.
9. It is further submitted that though the incident had taken place on 23.09.2022, she lodged a complaint against the petitioner on 14.09.2023 after lapse of one year which she did not explain.
The delay in lodging the complaint would indicate that a false complaint has been set up by the petitioner.
Hence, the petition may be allowed.
10. In support of his contention, the learned counsel relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJNISH SINGH @ SONI v. STATE OF U.P AND ANOTHER1.

entities.text: RAJNISH SINGH @ SONI v. STATE OF U.P AND ANOTHER1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

11. Per contra, the learned HCGP for respondent No.1 - State vehemently opposed the said submissions and he further 2025 Live Law (SC) 279 NC: 2025:KHC-K:1524 submitted that the complainant being a woman had been subjected to rape on the pretext of false promise of marriage.

The averments of the charge sheet have to be tested through the full pledged trial.
12.
It is further submitted that the petitioner has induced her on the promise of marriage and committed rape.
Thereafter, he induced her to obtain divorce from her first husband.
After having obtained the divorce, she requested him to marry her.
He refused to marry her, therefore, she lodged a complaint.
The delay might have been caused due to false promise made by the accused/petitioner.
Hence, it is not appropriate to quash the charge sheet.
Making such submissions, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.

13. Similarly, learned counsel for respondent No.2 adopted the arguments advanced by learned HCGP and he further submitted that the averments of the complaint would indicate that the matter requires full pledged trial.
Since there are direct allegations made against the petitioner, at this stage, it is not appropriate to quash the NC: 2025:KHC-K:1524 proceedings.
If the said proceedings are quashed, she would be put to irreparable loss and hence, the petition has to be rejected in order to secure the ends of justice to her.
As such, he prays to dismiss the petition.

14. Heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of the averments of the charge sheet, it appears from the records that the petitioner has been acquainted with the complainant through accused No.2.

He is said to have promised the complainant that he would marry her and called her to Manvi on the pretext of giving an order to do make-up work to the bride and family members and kept her in the hotel room on that night and stated to have committed rape by administering the intoxicating agent in the juice.

sentences.text: The complaint came to be filed by the complainant making certain allegations against the petitioner after lapse of one year.
On reading of the averments of the charge sheet, there is no proof that she had been subjected to rape and there is no proof that she had been administered intoxicating agent.
Even assuming that the petitioner had committed sexual intercourse with the NC: 2025:KHC-K:1524 complainant, it cannot be said that she cannot understand the consequences thereof.
Therefore, it can be inferred that she was the consenting party to the act.

16. In this context, it is appropriate to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajnish Singh @ Soni stated supra, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph No.34 held as under:
"34.
It is trite that there is a distinction between rape and consensual intercourse.

This Court in Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana, differentiated between a mere breach of promise and not fulfilling a false promise and held that an accused will only be liable if the Courts Concludes that his intentions are mala fide and he has clandestine motives.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is reproduced hereinbelow:-
"21.
Consent may be express or implied, coerced or misguided, obtained willingly or through deceit.
Consent is an act of reason, accompanied by deliberation, the mind weighing, as in a balance, the good and evil on each side.

There is a clear distinction between rape and Consensual sex and in a case like this, the court must very carefully examine whether the accused had actually wanted to marry the victim, or had mala fide motives, and had made a false NC: 2025:KHC-K:1524 promise to this effect only to satisfy his lust, as the latter falls within the ambit of cheating or deception.
There is a distinction between the mere breach of a promise, and not fulfilling a false promise.

Thus, the court must examine whether there was made, at an early stage a false promise of marriage by the accused; and whether the consent involved was given after wholly understanding the nature and consequences of sexual indulgence.

There may be a case where the prosecutrix agrees to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused, and not solely on account of misrepresentation made to her by the accused, or where an accused on account of circumstances which he could not have foreseen, or which were beyond his control, was unable to marry her, despite having every intention to do so.
Such cases must be treated differently.
An accused can be convicted for rape only if the court reaches a conclusion that the intention of the accused was mala fide, and that he had clandestine motives.

24. Hence, it is evident that there must be adequate evidence to show that at the relevant time i.e. at the initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever,
of keeping his promise to marry the victim.

There may, of course, be circumstances,
when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the NC:
2025:KHC-K:1524 victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.
The "failure to keep a promise made with respect to a future uncertain date, due to reasons that are not very clear from the evidence available, does not always amount to misconception of fact.

4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "misconception of fact
", the fact must have an immediate relevance".

Section 90 IPC cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning, the accused had never really intended to marry her."
(emphasis supplied)
17.
On careful reading of the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it makes it clear that there is a clear distinction between rape and consensual sex.

18. In the present case, though the petitioner stated to have committed rape on the complainant/victim on the pretext of false promise of marriage, the fact remains that, as on the date of alleged incident, she was divorced from her first husband and she did not lodged a complaint immediately after the incident.
As the complainant did not lodge a complaint after the incident, it can be inferred that she was consenting party to the sexual act committed to her.
Even on reading the entire charge sheet, it would not be possible to record conviction.
Hence, it is appropriate to quash the proceedings.

20. In the light of the observation made above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
ii) The entire charge sheet and further proceedings in S.C No.140/2023 (Crime No.75/2023) pending on the file of learned Principal Sessions Judge at Raichur, are hereby quashed.
